title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Bakersfield, CA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Kern County oilfield, refinery, structural steel, DSA school and Caltrans work: Part C choice, Part B travel, eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Bakersfield: Six Days for Kern County Oilfield, Refinery, Structural Steel and Public Works Inspectors
html:
Kern County welds for three different masters. The oil fields around Bakersfield still need steam lines, flowlines, tanks and production facilities built and repaired. Two refineries in the Bakersfield area, one running crude and one converted to renewable diesel, keep maintenance and turnaround crews working. And the Central Valley's schools, highways, warehouses and public buildings are steel structures inspected under California rules that spell out the inspector's credentials: the state asks for a Certified Welding Inspector by name on state school projects and expects certified inspectors on Caltrans work. A welder or fitter in Bakersfield who wants to move into inspection will find that the AWS CWI opens doors in all three.

Atlantis NDT offers a six-day course that prepares Kern County candidates for the CWI examination: field welders, fabrication shop QC staff, testing lab technicians, NDT technicians and engineers. AWS writes and administers the examination and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to AWS on their own and meets its eligibility and vision rules personally. Atlantis prepares people; it has no AWS approval or endorsement and no sight of the exam's questions. There is no Atlantis classroom in Bakersfield. The course runs online at the candidate's own pace with an instructor answering questions, at an employer's facility for a group, or one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Each of the six days is described on the national AWS CWI course page.

Heavy oil, steam and the welds behind it

North-northeast of Bakersfield, in the lower Sierra foothills, the Kern River field is one of the largest oil fields in the United States and is described as the most densely developed field in California. Chevron is the principal operator, and enhanced recovery methods such as steam flooding made it possible to produce oil once considered uneconomic to extract. Fields like this run on welded steel: steam generation and distribution piping, produced fluid lines, separation and treating equipment, tank farms and the structural supports that carry all of it. Much of that work is repair and replacement rather than new construction, and repair welds need inspection as much as new ones.

California regulates that equipment closely. The Geologic Energy Management Division, CalGEM, regulates oil and gas pipelines between the wellhead and the sales meter under Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, Sections 1774 through 1774.2 for construction, testing and maintenance. Aboveground pipelines must be inspected for leaks and corrosion every year, new, repaired or modified lines must be tested before they go back into service, and operators keep pipeline management plans that map lines near sensitive areas. Production tank shells must have their wall thickness tested every five years. The Office of the State Fire Marshal regulates certain crude oil pipelines, mostly outside field boundaries. A CWI on an oilfield contract is the person who checks that the repair welds behind those tests were made right in the first place.

In practice that means a routine that changes little from one lease to the next. Before a repair crew starts, the inspector confirms which welding procedure applies, that each welder holds a current qualification for the process, position and pipe size, and that the replacement pipe and fittings match the material called for. During the job the inspector checks bevels, fit-up and alignment, watches the root pass where access allows, and examines every completed weld for profile, undercut, porosity, cracks and arc strikes. Afterwards the paperwork has to tie each weld to the welder, the procedure and the test that followed, because a CalGEM inspector or the operator's integrity group may ask for it years later.

Refining in Kern County, crude and renewable

Kern Oil & Refining, which operates as Kern Energy, runs a refinery on East Panama Lane that can process up to 25,000 barrels of crude a day into gasoline and diesel, and also makes biodiesel from vegetable oil and tallow. The site has refined oil since 1934, when it opened as El Tejon Oil and Refining. Elsewhere in Bakersfield, the former Alon refinery, a 70,000-barrel-a-day crude plant that had been idled, was bought by Global Clean Energy Holdings in 2020 and rebuilt to make renewable diesel, with no petroleum processing; the company declared it commercially operational in December 2024. After a Chapter 11 reorganization in 2025 the business emerged as Grapevine Energy.

Plants like these keep pressure equipment integrity teams busy. An April 2026 Grapevine Energy posting in Bakersfield for a pressure equipment integrity inspector at the Central Valley Renewable Fuels refinery listed the CWI alongside API 510, 570 and 653 and Level II NDE certifications as preferred, and described weld quality control and verification of contractor qualifications as part of the job. For refinery maintenance and turnaround work the welding is largely to ASME B31.3 for piping and to the pressure vessel codes, with procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX.

Structural steel and seismic detailing

Bakersfield has a long-established structural steel trade. Kern Steel Fabrication, founded in 1959, fabricates structural steel for Central and Southern California and also designs and builds aircraft ground support equipment. A recent quality control posting from the company referenced AISC 207-20, ISO 9001:2015, AWS D1.1:2020 and AWS D1.8:2021, and asked for three to five years of welding or fitting experience or a CWI. AWS D1.8 is the structural welding seismic supplement, and its appearance in a Bakersfield job ad is a reminder that steel frames in a seismic state can include demand-critical welds and extra requirements that inspectors must know alongside D1.1.

Testing and inspection firms carry much of the field load. BSK Associates, recruiting in Bakersfield for welding inspectors and special inspectors, listed ICC certifications in structural steel, concrete, masonry and fireproofing, ACI technician certification, AWS CWI and Caltrans field and laboratory certifications among the credentials to hold or acquire, with projects spread across Kern, Tulare, Kings, Fresno, San Luis Obispo, Monterey and Los Angeles counties. Inspectors in that role work from the California Building Code, the International Building Code and ASTM, ACI and AWS standards, and write daily field reports and nonconformance reports.

School projects, highways and two rulebooks that name the inspector

California's Division of the State Architect (DSA) oversees construction of public K-12 schools, community colleges and state-owned or state-leased essential services buildings. Its interpretation of regulations on structural welding inspection, IR 17-3, says the inspector must hold AWS certification as a CWI or Senior CWI, or a Canadian Welding Bureau Level 2 or Level 3 certification, must be at least 25 years old, must have at least three years of relevant construction or inspection experience, and must know the special welding inspection requirements in Title 24. It applies to shop and field welding alike, and it adds that nondestructive testing on those projects must be done by Level II personnel employed and supervised by a laboratory DSA has evaluated and approved for the purpose. The version reviewed here was revised in May 2018, so check DSA's current edition before relying on the details. Kern County's school districts and community colleges build under that regime, and an inspector without one of those credentials cannot fill the role.

Caltrans takes a similar line on highway structures. Its construction manual tells resident engineers to confirm that the contractor has assigned a qualified quality control manager and inspection personnel, that nondestructive testing is done by certified welding inspectors and testing inspectors, and that welding follows an authorized welding quality control plan, with no welding on permanent work until the submittals are authorized. Steel bridge work under Caltrans is the natural home of AWS D1.5.

Choosing a code book for Part C

Part C of the examination is an open-book test on one code chosen at application, and Kern County candidates split along the lines of their work. AWS D1.1 suits structural fabricators, steel erectors and special inspectors on school and commercial buildings; D1.8 is not a separate Part C option, but D1.1 is the base it supplements. AWS D1.5 suits people at bridge fabricators and on Caltrans structures. The ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, suits refinery maintenance staff and inspectors on oilfield piping and pressure equipment. API 1104 suits pipeline construction inspectors. East Kern's aerospace cluster around the Mojave Air and Space Port, home to commercial spaceflight companies such as Scaled Composites, gives a few candidates a reason to consider AWS D17.1 for aerospace fusion welding. Background reading: AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, ASME B31.3 and ASME Section IX.

The AWS Kern Section and local welding education

Bakersfield has its own AWS section, the Kern Section, Section 170. In March 2026 it helped run an Industrial Trades Skills Competition for students at the Kern High School District's Regional Occupational Center, inviting members to judge, volunteer and staff a booth, and in May 2026 it held a member meeting in Bakersfield to elect its board for 2026-27. Taft College held its eighth annual AWS Welding Open House in April 2026. For Kern County candidates the section is the obvious place to meet working CWIs and to hear which contractors and labs are hiring. North of the county line, the AWS Central Valley Section covers Fresno, Kings, Tulare and neighboring counties.

Bakersfield College, at its Panorama campus, offers an Associate of Science in Welding, a Certificate of Achievement and a set of job skills certificates, among them welding certification, blueprint reading and layout, one covering gas metal arc, gas tungsten arc and flux cored welding, and one for shielded metal arc welding. The Regional Occupational Center's welding program serves high school juniors and seniors as well as adults, offers testing toward AWS D1.1 and an ASME Section IX pipe test, and articulates with Bakersfield College for credit. A welding education shortens the AWS experience requirement only if AWS classes it accordingly, so keep transcripts and certificates with your application papers.

Sitting the exam from Bakersfield

AWS requires at least 72 percent on each of the three parts. Fundamentals and Code Application are computer-based and booked at a Prometric test center once AWS has accepted the application and issued an eligibility code; Prometric's locator shows the nearest centers. Part B, the practical, runs only where AWS holds its CWI seminars. The AWS training locations page in November 2026 listed two California cities, Los Angeles and Sacramento, and Bakersfield candidates usually find Los Angeles, a couple of hours south over the Grapevine, the easier trip. Book the practical early, then fit the computer-based parts around it.

Six days, three formats, Kern County schedules

Oilfield maintenance crews, refinery staff and special inspectors rarely keep regular hours, and special inspectors may drive two hours to a jobsite before starting work. For them the online format is the practical choice: the six-day outline becomes a study plan with course notes, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and an instructor answers questions by message whenever they arrive. A fabricator, oilfield service company or testing lab preparing several people can host the corporate format at its own facility, where the practical day uses the company's own weld samples and gauges and the code day concentrates on the book the group works to. A single candidate who has failed one part, or who wants personal coaching on D1.1 or the ASME documents, can book the six days one-to-one.

The free NDT practice tests cover the testing topics in Part A, the Practical NDT welding workshop rehearses visual inspection steps in a browser, and the CWI exam budget planner helps set aside the AWS fees.

Experience, vision and the AWS application

AWS eligibility, set out in its QC1 specification, trades education against verifiable welding-related work. The requirement is one year with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, two years with an associate degree in welding, engineering technology, engineering or a physical science, four with completed trade or vocational courses, and five with a high school diploma or an approved equivalent, rising for less schooling. Oilfield roustabouts and helpers should be honest about which part of their work involved welding or weld inspection, because AWS decides what counts. Keep names, dates and a contact who can confirm each job.

The AWS visual acuity form calls for near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with correction permitted, and a color perception test performed by a qualified eye-care or medical professional, recent enough for the exam date. If you are aiming at DSA school work, remember that its experience and age requirements sit on top of the AWS rules rather than replacing them. More detail is in the CWI requirements guide.

After the CWI in Bakersfield

Special inspectors usually add ICC categories, and many add NDT. Performing ultrasonic, magnetic particle or penetrant testing needs method training and certification by the employer under its written practice; Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training, and the employer certifies the technician afterwards. Refinery inspectors often move toward API 510 and 570, which API administers and certifies. Local pages: ultrasonic testing in Bakersfield, magnetic particle inspection in Bakersfield, third-party inspection in Bakersfield, refining NDT consulting in Bakersfield and corporate NDT training in Bakersfield.

When you contact us, say which format suits you, how many people are involved, the Part C code each plans to use and when they hope to test; for an on-site group, add the facility and the weeks that work around production. Pricing depends on the format, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Bakersfield?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS Kern Section, Section 170, is based in Bakersfield; in 2026 it helped run a student skills competition at the Kern High School District's Regional Occupational Center and held its board elections in May. The Central Valley Section covers the counties to the north.

faq.q: Do California school projects require a CWI?
faq.a: DSA's interpretation of regulations IR 17-3, in the version revised in May 2018, requires structural welding inspectors on DSA projects to hold AWS CWI or Senior CWI, or CWB Level 2 or 3, plus at least three years of relevant experience. Check DSA's current edition.

faq.q: Which Part C code book suits Kern County work?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 for structural fabrication and special inspection, AWS D1.5 for bridges and Caltrans structures, the ASME option for refinery and oilfield piping, and API 1104 for pipelines. Pick the code you will work from every day.

faq.q: Where do Bakersfield candidates take Part B?
faq.a: At a location where AWS holds its CWI seminars. In November 2026 the California sites listed by AWS were Los Angeles and Sacramento, and Los Angeles is usually the shorter trip. Fundamentals and Code Application are booked separately with Prometric.

faq.q: Does AWS D1.8 appear on the CWI exam?
faq.a: D1.8, the structural welding seismic supplement, is not one of the Part C code options AWS lists. Candidates working on California steel frames usually test on AWS D1.1, the code D1.8 supplements, and learn the seismic requirements on the job.

faq.q: Can an oilfield service company host the course?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to your yard or shop for a group, using your gauges, weld samples and qualification records. Each person still applies to AWS individually and meets the eligibility and vision rules personally.

faq.q: I studied welding at Bakersfield College. Does that shorten the experience requirement?
faq.a: Possibly. AWS lists two years of welding-related experience for an associate degree in welding and four for completed trade courses, against five for a high school diploma, but AWS decides how a program is classed. Keep your transcripts.

faq.q: Is the Atlantis course approved by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has never seen exam content. AWS administers the CWI examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: What comes after the CWI for a Kern County inspector?
faq.a: Special inspectors often add ICC categories and NDT methods; refinery inspectors look at API 510 and 570. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training; see NDT training in Bakersfield.

faq.q: How do I ask for a quote?
faq.a: Send the format, headcount, Part C code and rough exam timing through the Bakersfield enquiry form. Each request is quoted individually, and we reply within one business day.
